intro: The cradle of democracy: the Acropolis above, lively neighbourhoods and rooftop bars below.
areas: Flea market, street food and bars.
sights: Book timed tickets and go early.
Sculptures and a glass floor over excavations.
Marble stadium of the first modern Olympics.
arrive: Athens International Airport is linked by Metro, suburban rail and express buses. Piraeus port has ferries to the islands.
around: Metro, trams and buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: Athens transport tickets, 24-hour and 5-day passes; tourist ticket includes the airport.
when: April–June and September–October; summer is very hot.
tip: Visit ancient sites at opening time in summer.

intro: Greece’s second city: a seafront promenade, Byzantine churches and the country’s best food scene.
areas: Bars and tavernas in old warehouses.
Upper town with walls and views.
night: Bars and tavernas in old warehouses.
Bars and clubs in a former trade district.
arrive: Thessaloniki Airport is linked by bus. Trains run to Athens.
around: Buses and the new Metro line; walkable centre.
tip: Walk the waterfront to the Umbrellas sculpture at sunset.

intro: Cycladic cool: whitewashed lanes, windmills, beach clubs and legendary nightlife.
sights: Sacred island and World Heritage site.
night: Sunset cocktail bars by the water.
arrive: Mykonos Airport has flights from Athens and Europe. Ferries sail from Piraeus and Rafina.
around: KTEL buses, taxis (limited) and boats to beaches.
pass: Buy bus tickets per journey; check current options.
when: Late May–June and September; July–August busiest.
tip: Taxis are scarce; book transfers ahead.

intro: A volcanic caldera island of white villages, sunsets and volcanic beaches.
eat: Crisp white wine from volcanic soil.
night: Beach bars on the black sand.
arrive: Santorini Airport is linked by bus and taxi. Ferries arrive at Athinios port.
around: KTEL buses; a hire car or quad helps.
pass: Buy bus tickets per journey; check current options.
tip: Cruise-ship days crowd Fira and Oia; check the schedule.

intro: Greece’s largest island: Minoan palaces, gorges, Venetian harbours and beaches.
areas: Venetian harbour, lighthouse and old town.
Capital, Knossos and the archaeological museum.
Venetian fortress, old town and long beach.
sights: Bronze Age Minoan palace near Heraklion.
Long hike through a national park (open in season).
Lagoon and pink-tinged sand beaches in the west.
eat: Barley rusk with tomato and cheese.
Grape spirit, often offered after meals.
arrive: Heraklion and Chania airports. Ferries from Piraeus.
around: KTEL buses; a hire car helps.
tip: Start Samaria Gorge early; check opening dates.

intro: A green Ionian island with a Venetian-British old town and beautiful bays.
areas: World Heritage old town with Venetian, French and British influences.
West-coast bays and a hilltop monastery.
sights: Arcaded promenade facing the Spianada square.
Palace built for Empress Elisabeth (Sisi) of Austria.
Boat trips to sea caves from its bays.
eat: Veal in white wine and garlic sauce.
night: Bars and cafés in the old town.
The island’s party resort in the south.
arrive: Corfu Airport is near the town. Ferries to Italy and the mainland.
around: Green and blue buses; hire car.
pass: Bus tickets per journey; check current options.
tip: Watch planes land by the Kanoni viewpoint.

intro: A sunny Dodecanese island with a medieval walled city and Lindos’ acropolis.
areas: World Heritage medieval city of the Knights.
sights: Restored palace of the Knights of St John.
Clifftop ruins with views over the bay.
eat: Harbour tavernas in Rhodes Town and Lindos.
night: Bars and clubs near Elli beach.
arrive: Rhodes Airport is linked by bus. Ferries to other islands.
around: KTEL and RODA buses; hire car.
pass: Bus tickets per journey; check current options.
tip: Visit Lindos early before day trips arrive.

intro: A sunny island nation of knights’ fortresses, megalithic temples and turquoise water.
areas: Baroque World Heritage capital, small enough to walk.
Seafront hotels, shopping and Paceville nightlife.
The fortified ‘Silent City’ and its neighbour.
sights: Baroque interior with Caravaggio’s Beheading of St John.
Walled medieval city on a hilltop.
Clear water reached by boat; very busy in summer.
eat: Flaky ricotta or pea pastries from small shops.
Maltese bread, often filled with tuna, capers and tomatoes.
night: Malta’s main club district in St Julian’s.
Historic street of bars and live music.
Summer saints’ festivals with fireworks and bands.
arrive: Malta International Airport is linked by bus. Ferries to Gozo.
around: Malta Public Transport buses cover Malta and Gozo; ferries cross the harbour from Valletta to Sliema and the Three Cities.
pass: Tallinja card and Explore cards for visitors; check current fares.
tip: Take the short harbour ferry from Sliema to Valletta instead of the bus.

intro: Cyprus’s party resort with white-sand beaches and sea caves.
areas: The main square and surrounding streets, packed with bars and clubs in summer.
Shallow turquoise water and a sandbar islet, a short walk west of town.
Protected headland of sea caves and coastal paths to the east.
sights: One of Cyprus’s best-known beaches; busy in high season.
Sea caves, cliff paths and the ‘Lovers’ Bridge’ rock arch.
Venetian-era monastery in the centre, which gave the town its name.
Open-air park of works by international sculptors near the sea.
eat: A long parade of small dishes; come hungry and share.
night: Clubs and bars around the centre, at their busiest in July and August.
Daytime and evening events at Nissi and nearby beaches in summer.
Harbourfront bars and restaurants for a slower evening.
arrive: Larnaca Airport is about 45 minutes away.
around: Intercity and local buses link Ayia Napa with Protaras and Larnaca; a hire car helps for Cape Greco (drive on the left).
pass: Local bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
tip: Walk or swim at Konnos Bay below Cape Greco for clearer, calmer water.

intro: World Heritage mosaics, a harbour castle and the birthplace of Aphrodite.
areas: The harbour area with hotels, the castle and the archaeological park.
The upper town with the municipal market and craft shops.
Sandy bay north of town with restaurants and watersports.
sights: World Heritage Roman villas with famous floor mosaics.
Rock-cut underground tombs by the sea.
The legendary birthplace of Aphrodite, east of town.
Small medieval fort at the end of the harbour.
eat: Fish or meat meze at the harbour and in the villages.
Sweet dessert wine from the Troodos foothills.
night: Clubs and bars in Kato Paphos.
Bars and tavernas along the promenade.
Open-air performances, including an opera festival at the castle in some years.
arrive: Paphos International Airport is about 15 km from town, linked by bus and taxi. Larnaca Airport is about 90 minutes away.
around: Paphos buses link the harbour, old town and Coral Bay; a hire car is useful for the coast and villages (drive on the left).
pass: Paphos bus day and weekly tickets; check current fares.
tip: Visit the mosaics and Tombs of the Kings early, before the midday heat.

intro: Cyprus’s cosmopolitan seafront city, with a castle, a marina and wine villages.
areas: Lanes around the medieval castle, with bars and restaurants.
Upmarket marina with restaurants and shops.
Long palm-lined promenade with sculptures and play areas.
sights: Medieval castle housing the Cyprus Medieval Museum.
Clifftop Greco-Roman city with a theatre over the sea.
Omodos and other villages in the hills.
Seafront walk between the old port and the city.
eat: Taverns in the old town and the hills.
Commandaria and village wines from the Troodos.
night: Bars and restaurants in the old town.
Traditionally held in early autumn; check dates.
arrive: Larnaca and Paphos airports are about 45–60 minutes away.
around: EMEL buses run along the seafront and to the suburbs; a hire car helps for Kourion and the Troodos villages (drive on the left).
pass: Bus day tickets are available; check current fares.
tip: Visit Kourion’s clifftop theatre late in the afternoon for the light and the views.
